requirement:
`habeas test` MUST run the full-workspace instrumented nextest workflow of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.run` and, only after that workflow succeeds,
run the post-suite check of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check`. It MUST
return a failing exit status if test execution, coverage collection, or the
post-suite check fails. It MUST NOT author exception evidence or invoke an
assessment model.
rationale:
The tests cover every obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.test`. The helper `full_flow` in `tests/execution_coverage.rs` runs `habeas test`. `saved_check` runs `coverage-check`, and `model_tripwire` sets up the model server.

- **Runs the instrumented nextest workflow, then the post-suite check.** `fn[full_test_flow_checks_real_function_counters_after_all_tests]` runs `habeas test` in a fixture workspace. It succeeds, and stdout contains "Coverage check passed". Exactly one saved run exists, with 4 attempts covering sync unit tests, an async tokio test and an integration target. Every attempt has non-empty function counters. So the full-workspace instrumented run happens and the check follows it. The fixture's nextest default filter is `kind(lib)`, yet the run still produces 4 attempts, so no-argument `habeas test` selects the whole workspace.
- **Fails when the post-suite check fails.** The same test then changes the sources so a nested function has zero execution. `habeas test` exits non-zero and stdout contains `#fn[outer]/fn[hidden]: zero execution`. The saved run's outcome is still "success", so the failure comes from the check and not from test execution. A later `coverage-check` also fails.
- **Fails on test failure and skips the check.** `fn[failed_suite_stops_full_flow_before_the_coverage_check]` uses a panicking test. The exit status is failing, stdout has no "Coverage check" text, and the saved outcome is "failed". This shows the check runs only after the workflow succeeds, and that test failure fails the command.
- **Fails on coverage collection failure and skips the check.** `fn[passing_tests_with_missing_or_corrupt_profiles_fail_collection_and_retain_partial_reports]` has tests that pass but write a missing profile or a corrupt profile. `habeas test` exits non-zero, stderr says partial profiles were retained, and stdout has no "Coverage check" text. The saved outcome is "failed" even though every test attempt succeeded.
- **Does not author exception evidence.** The full-flow test snapshots the `evidence` directory before the run. It asserts the contents are unchanged after both the passing and the failing `habeas test` runs, and after `coverage-check`.
- **Does not invoke an assessment model.** `model_tripwire` configures a local HTTP server as the authoring backend. The test asserts the request count is 0 after both the passing and the failing flows.

All three tests carry `{test}` references to `requirements.test-coverage.test`. I found no unmarked relevant tests and no untested obligation. The cited `run` and `check` requirements are context and I did not reassess them.
